title: India-Egypt Trade at $6.5 Billion Is 'Just a Beginning,' Goyal Says in Cairo
excerpt: On a visit with a 132-member business delegation, the commerce minister pitched two-way trade and investment — and asked the Indian community in Egypt to write a modern 'Periplus' business guide for the route.
body:
• Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal told an Indian community event in Cairo that India-Egypt bilateral trade of about $6.5 billion in 2025-26 is "just a beginning," urging a much bigger two-way partnership in goods, services and investment.
  • India exported $3.87 billion of goods to Egypt in 2025-26 against imports of $2.60 billion, while Egyptian FDI into India totals just $11.5 million since April 2000 — an imbalance Goyal wants Egyptian products and capital to help correct.
  • Goyal is travelling with a 132-member business delegation; more than 700 Indian companies are registered in Egypt, around 70 of them active, with combined investments above $5.5 billion.
  • For Indian exporters, the push names textiles, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, port infrastructure and logistics as the promising sectors in Egypt, which FIEO calls a gateway to African, Arab and European markets.

India and Egypt should set their sights on a far bigger trade partnership, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said in Cairo, telling an audience of Indian businesspeople and community members that bilateral trade of around $6.5 billion does not reflect the size of the two economies.

Goyal was addressing a community event hosted by the Indian Community Association in Egypt (ICAE) on Saturday evening, during a visit undertaken with a 132-member business delegation. His schedule includes meetings with Egyptian leaders and business representatives on ways to raise trade and investment in both directions, according to the Times of India.

"For the size of our two economies, I believe it's just a beginning; it cannot be our destination; the sky's the limit."

— Piyush Goyal, Commerce and Industry Minister

A two-way pitch, not just an export drive

The minister framed the visit as more than a sales trip for Indian goods. "We are looking at investment opportunities in Egypt; we are looking at marketing our goods and services... we are looking at Egyptian products coming to India and investments coming to India in areas of Egypt's strength, because ultimately trade has to be two-way. It has to be a win-win between the two nations," he said, in remarks reported by PTI.

The numbers explain the emphasis. India's exports to Egypt were $3.87 billion in 2025-26, against imports of $2.60 billion. Investment is far more lopsided: India has received just $11.5 million in foreign direct investment from Egypt between April 2000 and June 2026, while Indian companies have built a substantial presence on the ground in Egypt — more than 700 Indian companies are registered there, around 70 of them active, with combined investments exceeding $5.5 billion, according to the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO). India's main exports to Egypt include petroleum products, engineering goods, chemicals, cotton yarn, buffalo meat and pharmaceuticals; imports from Egypt include crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products.

Goyal also asked the ICAE to compile a practical business guide for companies in both countries. "Maybe you need to create a new 'Periplus' for businesses to engage between India and Egypt," he said, referring to the ancient guidebook of sea routes and trading ports.

Why Egypt, and what exporters are being told

The industry case, set out by FIEO ahead of the visit, is geographic. Egypt sits on the Mediterranean with a network of free trade agreements covering markets across Africa, the Arab region and parts of Europe, and India is already Egypt's fifth-largest source of imports. FIEO and trade analysts point to textiles, automobile manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, port infrastructure and logistics as the sectors where Indian investors and exporters have the clearest opening, including in Egypt's special economic zones along the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, as The Secretariat's briefing on the visit notes. Trade plumbing is also being built out: a Special Rupee Vostro Account opened by SBI with Banque Misr was operationalised in June 2026 to settle bilateral trade in rupees, and an Egypt Pavilion has been launched on the MSME Mart platform for smaller firms.

Part of a wider deal-making run

The Cairo stop sits inside a broader Indian trade offensive. Goyal told the audience that India has implemented trade agreements with Mauritius, Australia, the UAE, Oman, the EFTA bloc, New Zealand and the UK over the past five years, that an agreement with the European Union is scheduled to be signed next month, and that negotiations are under way with Canada, Chile, the South African Customs Union, Mercosur and the Eurasian Economic Union. Once those deals are counted, he said, Indian goods will have preferential access to markets representing $85 trillion of the world's $115 trillion GDP. The same push is visible in North America, where External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has said the India-US trade deal is near the "finishing line."

No bilateral trade target for Egypt was announced during the remarks. What exporters have instead is a direction of travel — a minister publicly calling $6.5 billion a floor rather than a ceiling, and a delegation on the ground looking for the deals to prove it.
